jobs.title: Principal Product Manager - Personalization
jobs.jd_full:
The Personalization team makes deciding what to play next easier and more enjoyable for every listener. From Blend to Discover Weekly, we’re behind some of Spotify’s most-loved features. We built them by understanding the world of music and podcasts better than anyone else. Join us and you’ll keep millions of users listening by making great recommendations to each and every one of them.

Spotify Search handles billions of queries across every market, language, and content type — music, podcasts, audiobooks, videos, playlists, and more. We’re looking for a Principal Product Manager to lead the Search Personalization within our Conversation Product Area, setting the product strategy for how hundreds of millions of users find and discover content on Spotify. This is a leadership role at the intersection of search systems, AI, and user experience. You’ll own the end-to-end strategy for search results — from ranking and relevance to AI-powered features like semantic search, LLM reranking, and AI Overviews — while leading two key Search squads (results ranking and query suggestions). Search is the front door to Spotify; this role shapes what people find when they walk through it.

What You'll Do

  • Set the product strategy and multi-cycle roadmap for Search Personalization at Spotify — spanning ranking, relevance, retrieval, AI-native features, quality, and trust.
  • Drive the evolution of Search toward AI-native experiences — AI Overviews, semantic search, LLM reranking — balancing innovation velocity with quality and cost discipline.
  • Own the Search quality bar: define how relevance, trust, compliance, and user experience connect into a holistic quality framework with measurable outcomes.
  • Manage Search’s role as a shared surface across many company strategies — build prioritization frameworks, communicate trade-offs, and represent Search at executive forums.
  • Influence and coach junior PMs working in Search.
  • Partner with engineering leadership to make architectural decisions that balance short-term delivery with long-term Search infrastructure health.
  • Drive cross-functional alignment where Search intersects.

Who You Are

  • You have 8+ years of product management experience, with 3+ years leading search, discovery, or information retrieval products at scale (100M+ users).
  • You have a deep technical understanding of search systems — ranking architectures, retrieval strategies, evaluation methodology, and the trade-offs between relevance, latency, cost, and freshness.
  • You have experience with AI/ML-powered search features — semantic search, LLM-based reranking, recommendations, or similar — and can lead a team through the transition from traditional to AI-native search.
  • You have a track record of managing complex stakeholder landscapes with competing priorities and limited resources, and can build frameworks for principled prioritization.
  • You think strategically at the portfolio level — you can synthesize across many concurrent initiatives, set a coherent vision, and communicate it clearly to executives.
  • You communicate with clarity and conviction, with the ability to translate technical complexity into compelling narratives for leadership, bet owners, and cross-functional partners.
  • You have experience mentoring and developing early-career PMs, and can influence without authority or direct reporting lines.
  • You bring familiarity with music, audio, or media technology and understand the unique dynamics of content-rich platforms.
  • You have experience operating Search as a platform that serves multiple internal teams or content verticals.
  • You have worked in content integrity, trust & safety, or regulatory compliance in the context of search or discovery systems.

Where You'll Be

  • This role is based in London or Stockholm.
  • We offer you the flexibility to work where you work best! There will be some in person meetings, but still allows for flexibility to work from home.

Compensation

Additional Information

Spotify is an equal opportunity employer. You are welcome at Spotify for who you are, no matter where you come from, what you look like, or what’s playing in your headphones. Our platform is for everyone, and so is our workplace. The more voices we have represented and amplified in our business, the more we will all thrive, contribute, and be forward-thinking! So bring us your personal experience, your perspectives, and your background. It’s in our differences that we will find the power to keep revolutionizing the way the world listens.

At Spotify, we are passionate about inclusivity and making sure our entire recruitment process is accessible to everyone. We have ways to request reasonable accommodations during the interview process and help assist in what you need. If you need accommodations at any stage of the application or interview process, please let us know - we’re here to support you in any way we can.

jobs.title: Senior Manager, Global Procurement (Materials)
jobs.jd_full:
ABOUT QUINCE

Quince is a destination for builders, creators, innovators, and operators who want to come together and challenge the status quo. Our mission is simple: make really high quality essentials for really low prices, fairly and sustainably. We deliver on that mission through a unique manufacturer-to-consumer (M2C) model eliminating the layers of traditional retail that add cost and result in consumers paying more than they need to. We find, build relationships with, and work directly with the manufacturing partners behind some of the world’s finest products. From there, our teams design smart, efficient operational processes and build and deploy proprietary technology, AI, and analytics to help us scale fast.

What began with a small assortment of elevated basics has quickly grown into a cross-category brand spanning apparel, accessories, home goods, and more. Today, tens of millions of people across a growing number of countries come – and return – to Quince because they trust us to deliver.

OUR CULTURE

Quince is a culture built for builders by builders. Our way of working starts with a blank sheet of paper. We question conventional thinking, use technology and data to uncover new opportunities, and move quickly to turn ideas into reality. We aren’t interested in replicating how others do retail. We’re building a better way – at a speed and scale unlike anything that’s been done before.

  • We dream big and chase the hard problems others shy away from. Rejecting long-held assumptions is part of our company's DNA. Where conventional wisdom says you have to choose – soft or durable, speed or rigor, quality or price – we ask why that trade-off has to exist in the first place.
  • Our pace is fast and the bar is high because our customers expect a lot from us and we refuse to let them down. We believe the best results come from challenging ourselves, learning from one another, and building on each other's strengths.
  • Here, responsibility is not determined by role, tenure, or seniority. Every team member - no matter their level - has the opportunity to drive our business and shape our trajectory.

If you’re someone who likes to imagine new possibilities and build better systems rather than plug-in to outdated ones, Quince is the place for you.

Open Roles

  1. Senior Manager, Global Raw Materials Procurement - Linen, Cotton & Other
  2. Senior Manager, Global Raw Materials Procurement - Cashmere & Silk
  3. Senior Manager, Global Raw Materials Procurement - Denim, Active & PKG Labels
  4. Senior Manager, Global Raw Materials Procurement - Leather & Down

THE IDEAL CANDIDATE:

We are looking for an exceptional Senior Manager, Global Procurement [Materials] to own and drive cost structures and savings. This role is critical to our goal of delivering the highest quality products, at radically low prices -done right. Reporting to the Head of Procurement, the ideal candidate will leverage their deep expertise in commodity costing, clean sheet, manufacturing excellence & efficiency, harvest timing, raw material availability to craft a competitive costing environment where T2 and T3 suppliers are being challenged to provide transparent, and competitive pricing to achieve a win win supply chain for both Quince and our partners.

Success in this role means achieving material cost at or near should-costing, below market indices, securing supply continuity, and contributing to product excellence by aligning material procurement with the company’s innovation and sustainability goals. This role offers the opportunity to make a significant impact on our business,contribute to company growth, and shape the future of our global procurement strategy.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Commodity Insights: Establish a monitoring framework to forecast global market shifts, raw material fluctuations, currency risks, and macro-material trends. Deliver actionable intelligence to procurement and leadership on a regular cadence.
    • Build and operationalize a live tracking system for key raw material prices, currency movements, and supply risks to proactively surface threats and opportunities.
  • Upstream Cost Engineering: Construct and scale material-specific clean sheets to lock in baseline component costs before finished-goods production. Provide the costing foundation for Tier 1 negotiations.
    • Build material-specific clean sheets for all top raw material inputs to create pricing transparency and support Tier 1 negotiation.
    • Support Buy Plan margin review to govern company margin target.
    • Partner with material sourcing team to ensure transparent, competitive pricing from all key material suppliers (we own material, we own costing)
  • Tier 2 (and Tier 3) Vendor Strategy: Map and design an upstream network strategy to consolidate raw material volumes across key material types and maximize direct-to-mill leverage. Reduce supply chain complexity while improving cost and availability.
    • Complete mapping of the Tier 2 and Tier 3 vendor landscape and deliver a defined material and vendor strategy that reduces complexity, ensures capacity, and increases direct-to-mill buying power.
    • Collaborate with cross-functional teams to integrate upstream material availability into product design and development cycles, ensuring early-stage cost optimization and seamless material-to-finished-good transitions.
  • Material RFPs: Design and execute RFPs tailored specifically to raw material vendors, yarn spinners/mills, tanneries, and textile mills. Own the full bidding process from vendor outreach through award.
    • Consistently deliver product exceptional material cost without sacrificing product quality or ESG considerations
    • Negotiate and execute immediate cost-reduction agreements directly with Tier 2 material suppliers, while simultaneously institutionalizing repeatable negotiation frameworks to build long-term material maturity and sustainable competitive advantage.
    • Partner directly with the Material Sourcing, Product Sourcing and Tier 1 and Tier 2 vendors to align on, and implement, material benefits into finished goods costing.
  • Value Creation: Identify and execute on opportunities to reshape the supply chain and extract new financial value beyond traditional sourcing boundaries, including verticalization and volume consolidation plays.
    • E.g. How do we become a market maker for Cashmere, Silk, etc? Could we sell cashmere and silk to other retailers? How can we partner with other mills or manufacturers to build a verticalized supply chain for critical materials, like linen, from French/Belgian farms and scutchers to linen mills? How do we buy/sell commodities to manage price fluctuations (e.g. gold pricing, Cashmere pricing)?

REQUIREMENTS:

  • 12-15 years of experience in raw material sourcing, commodity procurement, or upstream supply chain management
  • Deep knowledge of textile raw materials including yarns, fibers, fabrics, leather, and related commodities
  • Experience negotiating directly with mills, tanneries, yarn spinners, and raw material vendors
  • Familiarity with commodity hedging frameworks and global market indices
  • Proven ability to build and execute material-specific clean sheets
  • Strong analytical and financial modeling skills; comfort with large data sets
  • Technical aptitude for leveraging AI-powered platforms (e.g., LLMs) to conduct scenario analysis and automate complex procurement tasks.Experience in upstream supply chain network design or consolidation preferred
  • Experience working cross-functionally with merchandising, sourcing, and production teams
  • Bachelor’s degree required; MBA or advanced degree a plus

WHY QUINCE?

Joining Quince means being part of a mission-driven team reshaping retail. You will work alongside talented colleagues, tackle meaningful challenges, and contribute to building a more sustainable, accessible future for customers and partners alike.

EQUAL OPPORTUNITY & HIRING INTEGRITY

Quince provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applications for employment and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran or military status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local laws.

Quince is committed to providing reasonable accommodations to qualified individuals with disabilities. If you need a reasonable accommodation to complete your application or to perform the essential functions of a role at Quince, please let us know by completing this accommodation form. We review all requests individually and will work with you to determine appropriate accommodations on a case-by-case basis.

Employment is contingent upon successful completion of a background check. Quince will conduct background checks in compliance with applicable federal, state, and local laws.

Security Advisory: Beware of Frauds

At Quince, we're dedicated to recruiting top talent who share our drive for innovation. To safeguard candidates, Quince emphasizes legitimate recruitment practices. Initial communication is primarily via official Quince email addresses and LinkedIn; beware of deviations. Personal data and sensitive information will not be solicited during the application phase. Interviews are conducted via phone, in person, or through the approved platforms Google Meets or Zoom—never via messaging apps or other calling services. Offers are merit-based, communicated verbally, and followed up in writing. If personal information is requested to initiate the hiring process, rest assured it will be through secure and protected means.

jobs.title: Principal Product Manager - Format Foundations
jobs.jd_full:
We design Spotify’s consumer experience—end to end, moment to moment, across every screen, platform, and partner integration. Our mission is to make listening and watching feel effortless, personal, and joyful for hundreds of millions of users around the world. That means turning complexity into clarity across hundreds of touchpoints. If it touches a consumer, we shape it. We bring deep insight into human behavior, design, and technology to craft experiences that feel intuitive, expressive, and unmistakably Spotify.

We’re seeking a Principal Product Manager to help lead the consumer experience across Spotify’s formats, including books, podcasts, and music. Format Foundations partners with the business teams behind each format to lead innovation in how users discover, engage with, and build lasting relationships with content on Spotify. You’ll set the product vision and strategy for your area and shape feature portfolios across formats. This role sits within Format Foundations in Core Experience, partnering closely with these teams to grow their businesses through product innovation.

What You'll Do

  • Lead product vision and strategy across Spotify’s formats, shaping how books, podcasts, and music become more engaging, lovable, and valuable for users, creators, and the business.
  • Define and evolve the user experience across the content journey—from discovery and evaluation through engagement, library management, and retention.
  • Partner closely with business leaders across books, podcasts, and music to translate business strategy into product innovation that drives growth.
  • Drive innovation across multimodal and cross-format experiences, such as the intersection of listening and reading, and build capabilities that can scale from one format to others.
  • Work closely with engineering, design, data, and cross-functional partners to deliver high-quality experiences.
  • Use data, experimentation, and user insights to inform decisions and continuously improve the experience.
  • Align senior stakeholders across Core Experience, the business teams, and Personalization to create a cohesive consumer experience.
  • Lead multiple cross-functional initiatives end to end, owning scope and alignment and partnering with engineering on delivery.
  • Mentor product managers and raise the bar for product craft across the team.

Who You Are

  • You have 10+ years of experience in product management and have led product work across several consumer media products at scale in large technology companies.
  • You have deep knowledge of the consumer media landscape across areas such as books, podcasts, or music, including competitive dynamics, creator and publisher ecosystems, and user behavior.
  • You have experience building for mobile platforms such as iOS and Android, including complex user interfaces.
  • You understand how to build scalable systems and experiences that enable teams to move faster.
  • You’re able to balance user experience, technical constraints, and business impact.
  • You care deeply about creating intuitive, high-quality consumer experiences.
  • You’ve worked closely with engineering, design, and data partners to bring products to life.
  • You’re comfortable navigating ambiguity and bringing clarity across teams and organizations.
  • You’ve influenced senior leaders and stakeholders across functions and levels to drive alignment and outcomes.
  • You actively use AI tools in your product development workflow, from research and analysis to iteration and prototyping.

Where You'll Be

  • This role is based in Stockholm or London
  • We offer you the flexibility to work where you work best! There will be some in person meetings, but still allows for flexibility to work from home.

Compensation

jobs.title: Senior GTM Systems & AI Specialist
jobs.jd_full:
Who We Are

Cobalt was founded on the belief of a fundamental human aspiration: the desire to live better and safer. It all started in 2013, when our founders realized that pentesting can be better. Today our diverse, fully remote team is committed to helping organizations of all sizes with seamless, effective and collaborative Offensive Security Testing that empower organizations to OPERATE FEARLESSLY and INNOVATE SECURELY.

Our customers can start a pentest in as little as 24 hours and integrate with advanced development cycles thanks to the powerful combination of our SaaS platform coupled with an exclusive community of testers known as the Cobalt Core. Accepting just 5% of applicants, the Cobalt Core boasts over 500 closely vetted and highly skilled testers who jointly conduct thousands of tests each year and are at the forefront of identifying and helping remediate risk across a dynamically changing attack surface.

Cobalt is an Equal Opportunity Employer and we strive to build a diverse and inclusive workforce at our company. At Cobalt we aspire to engage with diverse individuals, communities, and organizations in order to continue to nurture our unique rich diverse culture. Join our team, and be your true self to do your best work.

Description

We are looking for a Senior GTM Systems & AI Specialist to own and scale the technology infrastructure that powers Cobalt’s go-to-market organization.

Reporting to the Sr. Director of Revenue Operations, this role will serve as the technical owner of our GTM technology ecosystem, with deep hands-on responsibility for Salesforce, HubSpot, integrations, enrichment, automation, and the systems supporting our customer lifecycle.

This is a highly cross-functional individual contributor role for someone who combines deep GTM systems expertise with a strong understanding of how modern B2B SaaS revenue organizations operate. You won’t just administer tools — you’ll partner with Revenue Operations, Marketing, Sales, Customer Success, and Analytics to translate business needs into scalable technical solutions and identify opportunities to leverage automation and AI to improve how our GTM teams operate.

Success in this role means our GTM teams have reliable systems, connected and trustworthy data, scalable automation, and an increasingly AI-enabled technology ecosystem that helps the business operate more efficiently.

What You'll Own

GTM Systems & Architecture

  • Serve as the primary technical owner and administrator of Salesforce, including architecture, objects, Flows, automation, permissions, integrations, data model, release management, reporting infrastructure, and system governance.
  • Own the broader GTM technology ecosystem, including integrations and data flows between Salesforce, HubSpot, Customer Success platforms, enrichment providers, prospecting and sequencing tools, and other GTM applications.
  • Partner closely with Revenue Operations to translate GTM strategy and business requirements into scalable technical solutions across Marketing, Sales, and Customer Success.
  • Evaluate, implement, and optimize GTM technologies with a focus on business impact, scalability, usability, and reducing operational complexity.

HubSpot & Marketing Technology

  • Serve as the primary technical owner and administrator of HubSpot, including workflows, lifecycle stages, lead scoring and routing, forms, campaign infrastructure, attribution configuration, integrations, automation, and data synchronization with Salesforce.
  • Partner with Marketing and Revenue Operations to ensure our marketing technology infrastructure supports lead management, campaign execution, attribution, intent signals, funnel measurement, and Marketing-to-Sales handoffs.
  • Maintain alignment between Salesforce and HubSpot data models, lifecycle definitions, routing logic, campaign data, and reporting requirements.

Data, Enrichment & GTM Signals

  • Own the technical infrastructure supporting GTM data quality and enrichment, including enrichment providers, field mapping, matching logic, deduplication, normalization, data governance, and ongoing monitoring.
  • Design and maintain reliable enrichment and data orchestration workflows that ensure GTM teams have accurate, complete, and actionable account and contact data.
  • Build scalable processes for activating intent signals, engagement data, enrichment signals, and buying triggers across GTM systems.
  • Proactively monitor data and integration health, identify gaps or failures, and implement solutions that improve data accuracy, coverage, reliability, and usability.

Customer Success Technology

  • Support the administration and integration of Customer Success platforms and the data infrastructure supporting the post-sale customer lifecycle.
  • Partner with Revenue Operations and Customer Success to enable processes such as customer health scoring, segmentation, account planning, renewals, expansion, churn risk, and lifecycle management.
  • Ensure customer and commercial data flows reliably across Salesforce, Customer Success platforms, and the broader GTM ecosystem.

Automation, AI & Innovation

  • Identify, design, and implement opportunities to automate repetitive GTM workflows across Marketing, Sales, Customer Success, and Revenue Operations.
  • Build scalable workflow automation using native platform capabilities, APIs, webhooks, and tools such as n8n, Zapier, or similar technologies.
  • Evaluate and implement practical AI-powered solutions that improve GTM productivity, research, data quality, prioritization, customer insights, or operational efficiency.
  • Build and experiment with AI-enabled workflows and agents where they can deliver measurable business value.
  • Stay current on emerging GTM and AI technologies and proactively recommend opportunities to improve how our revenue organization operates.

Systems Governance & Operational Excellence

  • Own system health, integrations, permissions, release management, documentation, and technical governance across the GTM technology ecosystem.
  • Establish monitoring and controls to proactively identify integration failures, data issues, workflow errors, and system risks.
  • Maintain clear documentation of architecture, integrations, workflows, business rules, and system dependencies to support scalability and business continuity.
  • Own technical initiatives end-to-end, from discovery and solution design through implementation, testing, deployment, and ongoing optimization.

You Must Have

  • 7+ years of experience in GTM Systems, Revenue Operations, Marketing Operations, Salesforce Administration, GTM Engineering, or a related field within B2B SaaS.
  • Advanced hands-on Salesforce administration expertise, including Flows, automation, permissions, integrations, data architecture, reporting, dashboards, and governance.
  • Advanced hands-on HubSpot administration expertise, including workflows, lifecycle management, lead scoring and routing, forms, campaigns, attribution, automation, integrations, and reporting.
  • Experience serving as a primary technical owner of Salesforce and HubSpot, including managing the integration and data flow between the two platforms.
  • Strong understanding of the end-to-end B2B SaaS GTM lifecycle across Marketing, Sales, and Customer Success, with the ability to understand business requirements and translate them into scalable technical solutions.
  • Strong experience with GTM data enrichment and governance, including enrichment providers, matching and mapping logic, deduplication, normalization, data quality monitoring, and CRM data management.
  • Experience designing and maintaining cross-platform integrations using APIs, webhooks, middleware, or workflow automation platforms.
  • Experience building scalable workflow automation using native GTM platforms and tools such as n8n, Zapier, Make, or similar technologies.
  • Experience administering or integrating Customer Success platforms and supporting post-sale customer data and workflows.
  • Experience applying AI and automation to GTM workflows, with an understanding of where AI can create meaningful business value and where traditional automation is the better solution.
  • Demonstrated ability to independently own business-critical GTM systems, troubleshoot complex issues, and drive technical initiatives from requirements through deployment.
  • Strong communication and partnership skills, with the ability to work effectively with Revenue Operations, Marketing, Sales, Customer Success, Analytics, and technical and non-technical stakeholders.

Nice to Have

  • Experience with GTM technologies such as Apollo, Clay, LeanData, ZoomInfo, 6sense, Gong, Outreach, Qualified, Clari, UserGems, Planhat, or similar platforms.
  • Experience designing signal-based GTM workflows using intent, engagement, enrichment, product, or customer data.
  • Experience building or deploying AI-powered workflows or agents within GTM systems.
  • Working knowledge of SQL, Python, JavaScript, TypeScript, or similar technologies used to extend and automate GTM systems.
  • Experience supporting a scaling SaaS organization through systems transformation, technology consolidation, or process redesign.

Why You Should Join Us

  • Grow in a passionate, rapidly expanding industry operating at the forefront of the Pentesting industry
  • Work directly with experienced senior leaders with ongoing mentorship opportunities
  • Earn competitive compensation and an attractive equity plan
  • Save for the future with a 401(k) program (US) or pension (EU)
  • Benefit from medical, dental, vision and life insurance (US) or statutory healthcare (EU)
  • Leverage stipends for:
    • Wellness
    • Work-from-home equipment & wifi
    • Learning & development
  • Make the most of our flexible, generous paid time off and paid parental leave

Pay Range Disclosure (For US openings only)

Cobalt is committed to fair and equitable compensation practices. The salary range for this role is ($135,000 - $160,000) + equity + benefits. A candidate’s salary is determined by various factors including, but not limited to, relevant work experience, skills, and certifications. The salary range may differ in other states and may be impacted by proximity to major metropolitan cities.

Cobalt (the "Company") is an equal opportunity employer, and we want the best available persons for every job. The Company makes employment decisions only based on merit. It is the Company's policy to prohibit discrimination in any employment opportunity (including but not limited to recruitment, employment, promotion, salary increases, benefits, termination and all other terms and conditions of employment) based on race, color, sex, sexual orientation, gender, gender identity, gender expression, genetic information, pregnancy, religious creed, national origin, ancestry, age, physical/mental disability, medical condition, marital/domestic partner status, military and veteran status, height, weight or any other such characteristic protected by federal, state or local law. The Company is committed to complying with all applicable laws and providing equal employment opportunities. This commitment applies to all persons involved in the operations of the Company regardless of where the employee is located and prohibits unlawful discrimination by any employee of the Company.

Cobalt is an E-Verify employer. E-Verify is an Internet-based system operated by the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) in partnership with the Social Security Administration (SSA). jobs.title: CX Operations Analyst
jobs.jd_full:
At ClickUp, we're building the future of work: the first truly converged AI workspace unifying tasks, docs, chat, calendar, and enterprise search, all supercharged by context-driven AI. We are an AI-native company. Every team member is expected to leverage AI daily, and we evaluate AI fluency as part of our hiring process. Join us and help redefine what's possible.

As a CX Operations Analyst, you will own key operational processes related to Partner Services (SOWs, invoicing, renewal processes, system access) while also providing data analysis, workflow automation, and AI builds that support multiple functions including TAM, Solutions and Support/CX. You are the person who keeps critical operational machinery running smoothly while continuously improving how it works.

This role works across the full CX Ops team and partners with stakeholders in TAM, Solutions, Support, Partner Services, Finance, and GTM Systems. You'll collaborate closely with other CX Ops team members on initiatives while taking direct ownership of your assigned processes and analytical deliverables. The right person for this role is detail-oriented, analytically strong, and energized by building automations and AI solutions that eliminate manual work. This role connects directly to our mission of making every CX team faster, better-informed, and more consistent through operational excellence. If you are an AI native, proactive, data-driven individual who thrives in a fast-paced environment, this role is for you!

jobs.title: Senior Product Manager, Mobile
jobs.jd_full:
Why Mozilla?

Mozilla Corporation is the non-profit-backed technology company that has shaped the internet for the better over the last 25 years. We make pioneering brands like Firefox, the privacy-minded web browser, and Pocket, a service for keeping up with the best content online. Now, with more than 225 million people around the world using our products each month, we’re shaping the next 25 years of technology and helping to reclaim an internet built for people, not companies. Our work focuses on diverse areas including AI, social media, security and more. And we’re doing this while never losing our focus on our core mission – to make the internet better for people.

The Mozilla Corporation is wholly owned by the non-profit 501(c) Mozilla Foundation. This means we aren’t beholden to any shareholders - only to our mission. Along with thousands of volunteer contributors and collaborators all over the world, Mozillians design, build and distribute open-source software that enables people to enjoy the internet on their terms.

About this team and role:

We’re looking for a hands-on Mobile Product Manager with a primary focus on Firefox for iOS, while also contributing across mobile (including Android).

This role is about building a better browser, turning downloads into loyal users, and creating experiences that truly stand out. What you'll bring:

jobs.title: Principal Product Manager, Agentic AI
jobs.jd_full:
Principal Product Manager, Agentic AI

REMOTE - US

JOB OVERVIEW

Legion is building AI agents that carry out workforce management work, not agents that describe it.

Much of what is presented as AI in workforce management today is a conversational layer over an existing scheduling screen. The more substantial problem — software that reasons over demand, labor regulation, and employee preferences, then acts, with a person in the loop wherever the stakes require one — remains unsolved across the category. Legion intends to solve it, and this role leads the product work to get there.

You will take an agent surface from operational research through specification, prototype, evaluation, and enterprise deployment, working hands-on throughout. You will work closely with Legion’s AI Lab engineers and with our CEO, who is engaged in this work daily.

RESPONSIBILITIES AND DUTIES

Agent definition. Determine what an agent is responsible for, which tools it may call, what it must escalate, what it must never do, and what a manager sees when it acts. These decisions affect employee pay and legal compliance. Much of this work is pre-launch, so you will shape the direction rather than inherit it.

Problem selection. The hardest judgment in agentic product work is identifying which workflows suit an agent and which do not. You will spend substantial time inside customer operations — district managers, store managers, labor operations, frontline employees — and return with a ranked, defensible view of where an agent creates measurable value and where it does not.

The human-in-the-loop contract. Scheduling decisions affect income, childcare arrangements, and legal protections. For each agent action you will define where autonomy is appropriate, the escalation thresholds, how a manager overrides the system, what is logged, and how a compliance team audits the outcome. Legion treats this as a first-class design problem.

Build quality. You are accountable for what ships, not for what was specified. That means staying engaged through implementation: reviewing the build against the specification as it comes together, using the product yourself before anyone else is asked to, joining bug triage and design review, catching drift from intent while it is still cheap to correct, and holding a release when the quality is not there. Our customers experience the build, not the document. A well-written specification that produced a product managers do not trust is failed product work, and we assess it that way.

Evaluation. Build and maintain the evaluation sets that determine whether an agent is ready to ship and whether it is degrading in production — writing the cases, reviewing failure traces, setting the pass criteria. You will be the person who holds a release when the demonstration is persuasive and the evaluation is not.

Specifications. Legion uses Functional Requirements Documents as its ground-truth specification layer; release notes, enablement material, and sales content are generated from maintained specifications rather than reconstructed from code or institutional memory. Write FRDs that meet that standard and keep them accurate after release. A specification is where the work begins, not where your responsibility ends.

Commercialization. Partner with go-to-market on packaging, metering, pricing inputs, and field readiness. Agentic products raise difficult commercial questions — what unit to meter, what a customer is paying for when software performs work a person previously did — and you will be expected to hold a considered position on them.

Design-partner delivery. Lead agent deployments with large enterprise design partners: scoping the pilot, establishing success criteria before it begins, joining failure reviews, and determining what becomes generally available and what remains bespoke.

TECHNICAL EXPECTATIONS

Legion is looking for a product manager who builds, rather than one who directs others who build. In a typical week, this role involves:

  • Writing and iterating on prompts and system prompts directly, and explaining why a change improved a behavior
  • Standing up a working prototype of a proposed agent — tool definitions, structured outputs, retries, guardrails — before engineering is asked to build anything
  • Using agentic coding tools (Claude Code or equivalent) daily: prototyping, data analysis, specification work, and reading the codebase behind your specifications
  • Reviewing an execution trace and diagnosing whether a failure originates in a tool description, a retrieval gap, a context-window constraint, an under-specified output schema, or a genuine model limitation
  • Building and running evaluation sets, and interpreting the results without a data scientist to translate them
  • Holding an informed position on retrieval design, tool-use patterns, structured output, model routing, latency and cost trade-offs, and multi-tenant safety in enterprise SaaS
  • Opening pull requests against our codebase — a prototype, a prompt change, an evaluation fixture, a specification stub. Pushing code is permitted and actively encouraged for product managers who want to work that way. It is not a requirement of the role, and the same review standards apply to everyone.
  • Following model releases, agent frameworks, and protocol changes, and translating them into roadmap implications within days rather than quarters

We recognize that this is a demanding technical bar for a product role. It reflects what the work actually requires.

REQUIRED SKILLS AND QUALIFICATIONS

  • 7+ years in product management (Senior) or 10+ years (Principal), including at least 2 years shipping LLM-backed features to external, paying users — not internal tools, proofs of concept, or hackathon projects
  • Demonstrated hands-on capability of the kind described above. Expect to show your work.
  • Substantial enterprise B2B SaaS experience: multi-tenant architecture, role-based access control, audit trails, single sign-on, data residency, security review, and enterprise procurement. You should be able to anticipate what a customer’s security questionnaire will ask about an LLM feature.
  • A record of taking an ambiguous, operationally complex domain problem through to a shipped product with demonstrated adoption — not only launch
  • Evidence of staying with a product through implementation and owning its quality at release. We will ask about a release you delayed or stopped, what you found, and how you found it.
  • The judgment to recognize what current models cannot do reliably, and the willingness to say so when a room expects a different answer
  • Comfort working inside a codebase. An engineering background is not required, but you should be able to read the code behind what you are specifying, run it locally, and open a pull request.
  • Strong written communication. Legion runs on documents, and candidates are evaluated substantially on how they write.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS AND ATTRIBUTES

  • Direct experience in workforce management, HCM, ERP, supply chain, or another operationally complex enterprise domain with compliance exposure
  • Familiarity with labor compliance regimes — predictive scheduling ordinances, meal and rest break rules, union work rules — or demonstrated ability to become fluent in a comparable regulatory domain quickly
  • Background in demand forecasting, optimization, or decision systems
  • Experience building platform or authoring surfaces that customers configure themselves
  • An engineering or technical degree, or prior experience as an engineer or data scientist
  • Experience with products sold into frontline-heavy industries: retail, hospitality, healthcare, or manufacturing

SCOPE OF ROLE, STATED PLAINLY

So that candidates can assess fit early:

  • This is an individual contributor role. There is no team to inherit and no management responsibility at present.
  • The role is accountable for what ships, not for what is specified. Writing the specification is a portion of the work, not the whole of it.
  • This is not an AI strategy or vendor-evaluation role. The work is product definition, prototyping, specification, evaluation, and delivery.
  • The role requires forming an independent point of view from operational research. Direction will not be handed down in detail.
  • The environment carries genuine ambiguity. The category is being defined as we work in it, and model capabilities shift underneath the roadmap.

SELECTION PROCESS

Our process includes a practical exercise: a sanitized workforce management problem, for which candidates produce an agent design — scope, tools, failure modes, human-in-the-loop contract, and evaluation plan — together with a working prototype they built themselves, using any model provider they prefer. The exercise is then discussed with the people the candidate would work alongside. We weigh it heavily, and we compensate candidates for the time.

COMPENSATION & BENEFITS

Salary Range: $280,000.00-$300,000.00 + Bonus + Stock Equity

At Legion, we offer competitive compensation and benefits packages to all employees. As a fully remote employer, pay for positions is determined using local, national, and industry-specific survey data.

Our posted salary range is done so in good faith based on national data and may be refined for a candidate’s region/town/cost of living. We strive to make competitive offers that allow employees room for future growth. Salaries will be based on the applicant’s location, level of experience, education, and specialized knowledge and skills. Additionally, we consider the external market rate, the amount we have budgeted internally, and the internal equity for the same position within the company.

Benefits include, but are not limited to:

  • $0 monthly premium and other flexible medical, dental, and vision plans effective on the first day of employment
  • 401k plan
  • Discretionary Paid Time Off and Paid Holidays
  • Parental Leave
  • Equity
  • Monthly Wellness Reimbursement
  • Monthly Lunch on Legion

ABOUT LEGION

Join Legion’s mission to turn hourly jobs into good jobs. We’re a remote, mission-driven team seeking exceptional talent to propel this vision. Embrace a culture that’s collaborative, fast-paced, and entrepreneurial. With us, you’ll grow your skills, work closely with experienced executives, and contribute significantly to our mission.

Legion Technologies delivers the industry’s most innovative workforce management platform. It enables businesses to maximize labor efficiency and employee engagement simultaneously. The award-winning, AI-driven Legion WFM platform is intelligent, automated, and employee-centric. It’s proven to deliver 13x ROI through schedule optimization, reduced attrition, increased productivity, and increased operational efficiency. Legion delivers cutting-edge technology in an easy-to-use platform and mobile app that employees love.

If you’re ready to make an impact and grow your career, Legion is where you belong. Join us in making hourly work rewarding and fulfilling.

BACKGROUND AND OPPORTUNITY

There are almost 75 million hourly workers in the United States, representing more than half of the entire workforce. Historically, managing hourly employees has been difficult due to high attrition (average of 60%) and high replacement costs (average of $3,200 per employee in retail). The ongoing labor shortage and competition from the gig economy make it more difficult to attract and retain hourly employees. The top reasons hourly employees leave their jobs are a lack of schedule empowerment, poor communication with employers, and an inability to get paid early. Gen Z and the millennial workforce demand gig-like flexibility, modern technology, and compelling work options. Legion’s mission is to turn hourly jobs into good jobs, serving the hourly workers who make up the majority of the US workforce. We believe in empowering employees and helping employers be efficient and innovative by enabling intelligent automation powered by Legion’s Workforce Management platform to optimize labor efficiency and enhance the employee experience simultaneously. Legion WFM was built for the cloud with AI at the core and designed to handle the complexity of modern businesses and meet the needs of today’s hourly employees.  Our team is comprised of dedicated individuals from all backgrounds and experiences, globally distributed across all time zones.

For more information, visit https://legion.co

EQUAL EMPLOYMENT OPPORTUNITY

Legion Technologies is proud to be an equal-opportunity employer and is committed to maintaining a diverse and inclusive work environment. All qualified applicants will be considered for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, age, disability, marital status, familial status, sexual orientation, pregnancy, genetic information, gender identity, gender expression, national origin, ancestry, citizenship status, veteran status, and any other legally protected status under federal, state, or local anti-discrimination laws.

DISABILITY ACCOMMODATION

For individuals with disabilities who need additional assistance at any point in the application and interview process, please email recruiting@legion.co

We have noticed a rise in recruiting impersonations across the industry, where scammers attempt to access candidates’ personal and financial information through fake interviews and offers. All Legion recruiting email communications will always come from the @legion.co domain. Any outreach claiming to be from Legion via other sources should be ignored. If you are uncertain whether you have been contacted by an official Legion employee, reach out to recruiting@legion.co

Legion is an equal opportunity employer. All applicants will be considered for employment without attention to race, religion, color, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, national origin, veteran, disability status, or any other basis covered by appropriate law.

How We Determine What We Pay

As a global employer, Legion determines pay for positions using local, national, and industry-specific survey data. We evaluate external equity and the cost of labor/prevailing wage index in the relative marketplace for jobs directly comparable to jobs within our company. Our posted salary range is based on national data and may be refined for a candidate’s region/town/cost of living. For new hires, we strive to make competitive offers allowing the new employee room for future growth. Salaries will be based on the applicant’s location, level of experience, education, and specialized knowledge and skills. Additionally, we consider the external market rate, the amount we have budgeted internally, and internal equity within the company for the same position. An employee/candidate with a stronger skill set will receive higher pay.

Job Applicant Privacy Policy

This Job Applicant Privacy Policy (“ Policy”) describes how Legion Technologies, Inc. (“ Legion”, “ we”, “ us” and “ our”) collects, uses, and discloses “personal information” as defined under California law from and about job applicants who are residents of California.

This Policy does not apply to our handling of data gathered about you in your role as a user of our consumer-facing services. When you interact with us as in that role, the Legion Privacy Policy applies.

  1. Types of Personal Information We Handle

We collect such information either directly from you or (where applicable) from another person or entity, such as an employment agency or consultancy, background check provider, or other referral sources. This information includes:

  • Education Information such as institutions attended, degrees, certifications, training courses, publications, and transcript information.

  1. How We Use Personal Information

We will also use job applicant information for internal analysis purposes to understand the applicants who apply and to improve our recruitment process. About the role

$75,000 - $85,000 a year

jobs.title: Senior Program Manager
jobs.jd_full:
MongoDB’s Incident & Escalation Management (IEM) function coordinates cross-functional responses to critical customer situations and drives improvements to how we respond over time. We’re looking for a Senior Program Manager to strengthen the function’s ability to deliver its program priorities consistently across regions through focused planning, disciplined execution, clear visibility, and dependable follow-through.

As an execution partner to IEM leadership, you’ll help turn strategic priorities and operational learnings into a measurable book of work. You’ll establish clear plans, ownership, operating cadences, risk visibility, and follow-through, while bringing an informed external perspective on relevant industry practices. You’ll partner with the IEM team and stakeholders across Technical Services, Engineering, Product, Customer Success, Sales, and other teams in the Americas, Asia Pacific, and EMEA.

This is a program-management role - not an incident commander or technical investigator role. Functional leaders and incident responders retain accountability for strategy, policy, technical decisions, people leadership, and live operational response. You’ll own the execution system around prioritized work so leaders and subject-matter experts can focus on customers, technical judgment, incident leadership, and their teams.

We are looking to speak to candidates who are based in Toronto for our hybrid working model.

What you’ll do

  • Own the IEM program of work and its supporting materials, maintaining a clear roadmap of outcomes, priorities, owners, milestones, dependencies, capacity considerations, commitments, and decisions
  • Partner with IEM leaders and sponsors to identify and prioritize strategic focus areas, assess opportunities to mature the function, and recommend practical improvements aligned with relevant industry practices
  • Turn ambiguous needs into scoped, measurable work. Clarify outcomes, sequence milestones, establish accountable owners, document decisions and delivery expectations, and coordinate technical and cross-functional reviews
  • Drive delivery across Technical Services, Engineering, Product, Customer Success, Sales, and partner teams. Clarify accountability and handoffs, resolve dependency gaps, and surface blockers, capacity constraints, and resourcing risks early—with options and recommendations
  • Establish and run planning, program-review, and risk-review cadences. Keep backlogs and program records current and decision-ready, track commitments, facilitate decisions, and follow agreed actions through closure
  • Connect IEM program works with the Customer Organization’s wider PMO, aligning planning, governance, dependencies, and reporting to ensure organizational alignment and visibility
  • Help translate recurring incident and escalation patterns, post-incident findings, customer-impacting gaps, and corrective actions into prioritized improvement work with owners, timelines, milestones, and verifiable closure criteria. Coordinate root-cause analysis completion and customer incident-report delivery with clear ownership and quality expectations
  • Advance incident-response and escalation practices, including frameworks and playbooks, readiness, communications, training, simulation exercises, post-incident review, and consistent implementation across teams and regions
  • Partner with data and tooling teams to improve operational instrumentation, metrics, reporting, workflow integration, and automation. Help ensure AI-enabled workflows are appropriately governed, measured, and human-reviewed.
  • Mature program reporting by refining outcome and health measures, improving data quality and consistency, establishing baselines, and turning operational data into actionable insights - not simply reporting activity or optimizing a single response-time metric
  • Prepare concise updates, requirements, specifications, operating proposals, decision records, and executive-ready summaries that make progress, trade-offs, risks, and decisions clear
  • Coordinate readiness and adoption so approved changes to processes, tooling, roles, communications, and operating procedures are understood, operationalized, and sustained

What success looks like

  • Priority initiatives have clear outcomes, accountable owners, realistic milestones, active risk tracking, and reliable follow-through
  • Leaders have an accurate, timely view of program health, delivery risks, dependencies, capacity constraints, and decisions needed
  • Post-incident and post-escalation learning becomes prioritized, durable improvement; corrective actions have clear owners and do not remain open-ended
  • Readiness, handoffs, communications, and closure practices become more consistent and measurable across teams and regions
  • Escalation Managers, Incident Commanders, and technical experts spend less time coordinating program work and more time applying their expertise to customers, incidents, and teams
  • Program measures guide decisions and improvement, while execution reliability and stakeholder confidence increase

How success will be assessed

The role will be evaluated on program health and operational outcomes - not meeting or status-report volume. Measures will be baselined during the first 60–90 days and refined with leadership. They may include:

  • The share of priority initiatives with clear outcomes, accountable owners, milestones, and active risk tracking
  • Initiatives and process improvements completed and adopted
  • Closure rate and aging of post-incident and post-escalation actions, overdue actions, and unresolved dependencies
  • Evidence that recurring incident and escalation patterns are being addressed through durable process, tooling, or product changes
  • Stakeholder confidence in visibility, coordination, and decision follow-through
  • Sampled estimates of coordination time returned to operational leaders and subject-matter experts

What you’ll bring

  • 7–10 years of progressive program or project management experience, with a track record of growing responsibility - from coordinating smaller initiatives to leading complex, cross-functional programs. Experience outside the technology sector is welcome
  • Significant experience leading complex, cross-functional programs in a global enterprise or similarly demanding environment, delivering through a matrix rather than relying on direct authority
  • Demonstrated experience with incident response, major-incident management, customer escalations, crisis management, service operations, trust & safety, or closely related operational programs at scale. You understand the lifecycle from detection and triage through coordination, communication, mitigation, review, and follow-through
  • A track record of building or improving operational programs - not only tracking projects - including governance, operating cadences, roles and handoffs, readiness, metrics, and continuous-improvement mechanisms
  • Strong project and program-management fundamentals, including program prioritization, scope and outcome definition, sequencing, dependency and risk management, capacity awareness, backlog discipline, stakeholder alignment, delivery governance, and change adoption
  • Experience establishing useful operating cadences and decision-ready reporting, and working with operational data to set baselines, interpret trends, and turn evidence into practical recommendations
  • The ability to structure ambiguous requests into clear requirements, operating proposals, decision records, and measurable work.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication, including concise updates for senior leaders and clear coordination across technical and customer-facing teams.
  • Sound judgment in high-pressure, ambiguous environments; a collaborative, calm approach to resolving blockers; and the ability to create accountability without adding unnecessary process.
  • Experience working across global teams, time zones, and organizational boundaries, and with program or delivery-management tools

Helpful experience

  • Experience in enterprise SaaS, cloud services, technical support, production operations, or another customer-facing technology organization
  • Familiarity with highly technical platforms, distributed systems, databases, reliability, or service-management practices
  • Experience with post-incident improvement programs, corrective-action tracking, operational dashboards, incident metrics, or executive reporting
  • Experience improving incident-management tooling, communications workflows, workflow automation, or responsibly governed AI-enabled operations
  • Experience coordinating global teams across regions, time zones, and follow-the-sun operating models

What you can expect in your first 90 days

  • First 30 days: Build relationships with sponsors, functional leaders, and program owners. Understand the operating model, active program work, commitments, decision forums, systems of record, reporting, and key measures
  • By 60 days: Reconfirm priorities, outcomes, owners, sequencing, dependencies, capacity constraints, and delivery expectations. Review risks, blockers, post-incident actions, and recurring coordination gaps; establish an initial baseline for program health and measures
  • By 90 days: Present a prioritized program overview, baseline assessment, risk and dependency summary, initial measure results, and recommendations for the next two quarters. Establish or strengthen the operating cadence, reporting, decision forums, and escalation paths

About Avalere Health

United by one profound purpose: to reach EVERY PATIENT POSSIBLE. At Avalere Health, we ensure every patient is identified, treated, supported, and cared for. Equally. Our Advisory, Medical, and Marketing teams come together – powerfully and intentionally – to forge unconventional connections, building a future where healthcare is not a barrier and no patient is left behind.

Achieving our mission starts with providing enriching, purpose-driven careers for our team that empower them to make a tangible impact on patient lives. We are committed to creating a culture where our employees are empowered to bring their whole selves to work and tap into the power of diverse backgrounds and skillsets to play a part in making a difference for every patient, everywhere.

Our flexible approach to working allows our global teams to decide where they want to work, whether in-office or at home based on team and client need. Major city hubs in London, Manchester, Washington, D.C., and New York, and smaller offices globally, serve as collaboration hubs allowing our teams to come together when it matters. Homeworkers are equally supported, with dedicated social opportunities and resources.

Our inclusive culture is at the heart of everything we do. We proudly support our employees in bringing their whole selves to work with our six Employee Network Groups – Diverse Ability, Family, Gender, LGBTQ+, Mental Health, and Race/Ethnicity. These groups provide opportunities to promote diversity, equity, and inclusion and to connect, learn, and socialise through regular meetings and programs of activity. We are an accredited Fertility Friendly employer with our Fertility Policy, enhanced parental leave, and culture of flexibility ensuring every employee feels supported across their family planning journey and can work in a way that suits their family’s needs.

We are deeply invested in supporting professional growth for our employees through day-to-day career experiences, access to thousands of on-demand training sessions, regular career conversations, and the opportunity for global, cross-capability career moves.

We take pride in being part of the Disability Confident Scheme. This helps make sure you can be interviewed fairly if you have a disability, long term health condition, or are neurodiverse. If you’d like to apply and need adjustments made, you can let us know in your application.

About the role :

The Associate Project Manager (or APM) will have project specific responsibilities & ownership of low/mid complexity projects across a set of client account(s) as assigned. They will work closely with their agency counterparts (Account, Creative, Finance, Strategy, Technology) to create the space for great ideas, work and results.

The role is accountable for achieving great project-level results for low/mid complexity projects (and supporting large scale projects with oversight) for the agency through thoughtful project planning, staff alignment and effective project management that anticipates and actively manages to mitigate risks. The APM will also begin to take on greater financial management responsibilities in the form of estimating work, monitoring budgets and supporting other agency financial processes.

What you’ll do:

  • Point of contact for client for low/mid complexity work that has been kicked off and is in motion at the agency
  • Solicit client direction and input; manage client expectations
  • Supports the organization and prioritization of work across client responsibilities
  • Consultative approach able to identify and mitigate project risks before they become issues
  • Ability to synthesize client interactions into actionable direction
  • Deliver high quality work that exceeds client expectations
  • Financial management including pricing, budget management, reconciliation, billing, and the ability to effectively communicate financial status/risks/mitigation plans to client
  • Actively partner with Account, Creative, Finance, Strategy and Technology to establish project approach and pull through the work from job activation to end delivery
  • Work closely with Account partners to clearly define and activate project work
  • Serve as organization hub for assigned clients and project work
  • Manage daily hot sheets, facilitate flow of project work, partner closely with resource management to align staff to the work
  • Facilitate efficient communication across the agency team including capturing meeting notes and outlining next steps as required
  • Create and manage project timelines and resource assignments
  • Developing decision maker and problem solver. Expanding ability to set direction for the team based on good, consistent decision making
  • Expanding financial management responsibilities including scoping/estimating work, budget management and supporting other agency financial processes
  • Prepare/support and lead client submissions
  • Ability to lead the scoping and estimation of low/mid complexity work
  • Monitors and assigns tasks to internal project team
  • Ability to run client and team meetings
  • Accountable for delivering revenue in the month projected
  • Works closely with their account management counterpart to ensure accurate financial projections.

About you:

  • 1 year of relevant experience, agency/pharma setting preferred
  • Ability to work well with cross functional teams
  • Extreme attention to detail
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills
  • Client facing abilities
  • Solid presentation skills

$55,000 - $70,000 a year

What we can offer

You will receive a 401K plan with an employer match contribution up to 4% (immediately vested), as well as life insurance, disability coverage, and medical, dental, and vision plans for peace of mind. Enjoy flexible working arrangements, including hybrid and remote work, along with the option to work from anywhere across the globe two weeks each year. We provide 20 vacation days plus one personal well-being day, recognise 9 public holidays, along with gifted end-of-year holidays and an early Summer Friday finish in June, July, and August.

Access free counselling through our employee assistance program and personalized health support. Our enhanced maternity, paternity, family leave, and fertility policies provide support across every stage of your family-planning journey. You can also benefit from continuous opportunities to professionally develop with on-demand training, support, and global mobility opportunities across the business.

We encourage all applicants to read our candidate privacy noticebefore applying to Avalere Health.

We may use AI tools to support elements of the hiring process, such as reviewing applications, analyzing CV/resumes, assessing responses, or transcribing interviews. These tools assist our Talent team but do not replace human judgment. Final hiring decisions are ultimately made by humans. If you would like more information about how your data is processed, please review our candidate privacy policy.
